sense: a way of looking at a matter

terms.gloss: look at, judge (a thing) from (a standpoint)
terms.grammar: spectō, spectāre, first conjugation, with ex + ablative
evidence: Ter. An. 646: quī tuum animum ex animō spectāvī meō
Cic. Tusc. 5.31: nōn igitur ex singulīs vōcibus philosophī spectandī sunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin has no noun for a perspective in this sense: the English word is a metaphor from drawing. Latin says what one judges a thing by, ex with spectāre (Lewis & Short: “to judge of”), or whose opinion it is (see opinion). Spectāre is first of all to look at, watch.

phrases.latin: heu mē miserum, quī tuum animum ex animō spectāvī meō
phrases.english: poor me, who judged your heart by my own

phrases.latin: nōn igitur ex singulīs vōcibus philosophī spectandī sunt, sed ex perpetuitāte atque cōnstantiā
phrases.english: so philosophers are not to be judged by single sayings, but by their consistency throughout

sources: Terence checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
